FAB-17.ruling: Option (b), ENGINE POSITION MERGES LAST, scoped by the ruling's own words to: 'the engine's POSITIONING BLOCK -- position, the placement coordinates it computes, and the z-index it owns -- merges after caller style on Modal, Drawer, and Dropdown's overlayStyle; caller style customizes everything else.'

implemented.Modal: `position` and the fullscreen `top/left` moved after `...style`. top/left are 'the placement coordinates it computes' -- inside the ruling.
implemented.Drawer: `position: fixed` and the owned `zIndex` moved after `...style`. The placement COORDINATES were already safe: the switch spreads `...base` then adds top/left/width/height, so they always outranked caller style. Only position and zIndex were exposed.
implemented.Dropdown: `position`, the owned `zIndex`, and the popup/in-tree coordinates moved after `...overlayStyle`.

FAB-17.minimizedToTheRuling: Dropdown's `visibility: 'hidden'` pre-measurement guard was initially carried into the merge-last block by the coordinates spread. `visibility` is NOT in the ruling's positioning block, so it was HOISTED back above `...overlayStyle` and remains caller-overridable. Narrowing caller semantics further than the ruling adjudicated would have been the implementer resolving scope again -- the exact move this round has repeatedly had to unwind.
callerVisibleFieldsDELIBERATELYleftOverr: every non-positioning property on all three
FAB-17.verification: Asserted programmatically for all four families: engine position appears AFTER the caller-style spread in Modal, Drawer and Dropdown. Popover reports n/a because it never sets position in that pattern -- it merges `positionStyle` last and is the protected control.
FAB-17.costLedgerEntry: Recorded honestly per the ruling: THIS FAILURE MODE DID NOT EXIST when the keyline painted on the element itself. The relocation to a pseudo created the positioned-ancestor dependency, and this ruling pays for it. POSITIONED-ANCESTOR INTEGRITY joins S, W and radius as a named property of the mechanism table.
FAB-17.stillOwed: Regression tests covering every caller-visible field, and the Chromium fixture (position:static injected via the public hatch, animation:none plus reduced-motion, asserting the keyline stays anchored, with Popover and the Dropdown submenu as protected controls). NOT YET WRITTEN. Until they exist this is implemented, not proven.

FAB-18.conditionI_NOT_YET_MET: The computed-parity probe across grounds AND under reduced-motion is NOT written. FAB-18.reducedMotionOBSERVATION: personality.css:934 sets `--ds-motion-attention: 0s !important`, so under that posture the dial computes to `calc(0s * 2)`. The skin independently declares `animation: none` under reduced-motion, so the duration is not reached -- but that is TWO mechanisms agreeing, and the parity probe must confirm it rather than infer it. Flagged for the probe, not resolved here.
FAB-18.conditionI_SPEC_REFINED: The probe must verify EACH MECHANISM INDEPENDENTLY: neutralize the skin's `animation: none` and assert the zeroed dial ALONE stops motion; then neutralize the dial and assert the skin rule ALONE does. Two mechanisms agreeing is not one mechanism verified. Same lesson as FAB-16's redundant resets, now in motion-space: overlapping safety is fine, UNCOUNTED overlap is how a load-bearing mechanism dies unnoticed later.

OWNERSHIP_VIOLATION_DISCLOSURE.MY_OWN_SHA_CONFLATION: Correction to this receipt's previous entry. I wrote that the SHAs I published were 'stale' and had been 'superseded' by the lane's. They were not superseded — they measure DIFFERENT THINGS. I published DIFF SHAs; the lane published FILE-CONTENT SHA256. I verified both against disk and they reconcile exactly. The correct record carries BOTH: the original diff SHAs as the baseline adopted FROM, and the content SHA256s as the adopted RESULT. Calling a different measurement 'stale' implied drift where there was none, and would have sent an auditor looking for a change that never happened.

INSTRUMENT_LESSON_MY_OWN_GLOB_CHECKER.what: I hand-rolled a glob-to-regex ownership checker to answer 'may I write this path'. It has now given a WRONG answer three times today.
theWrongAnswers: It reported the Modal/Drawer/Dropdown test paths as owned by the family lane and NOT by the quality-integrator. The authoritative matcher says the opposite: quality-integrator TRUE, family lane FALSE, for both `Modal/tests/x.tsx` and `Modal/engines/modern/tests/x.tsx`.

On that basis I told the adjudicator 'those paths are also the overlay lane's' and argued the tests should follow the implementation to one owner. The adjudicator corrected me. I now know WHY I was wrong, which the correction alone did not tell me.
It also mis-stated the relationship between diff SHAs and content SHAs earlier in this same receipt.
INSTRUMENT_LESSON_MY_OWN_GLOB_CHECKER.rootCause: `Modal/**/tests/**` requires an intermediate segment under my naive `**` -> `.*` conversion, so `Modal/tests/x.tsx` failed to match. The real matcher treats `**/` as matching zero or more segments. Glob semantics are not obvious and I reimplemented them badly.
INSTRUMENT_LESSON_MY_OWN_GLOB_CHECKER.theFix: STOP HAND-ROLLING IT. `laneScopeContains` is exported from scripts/quality-evidence/v2/ownership-overlap.mjs and is the authority the drills themselves use. Every future 'may I write this path' question goes through that function, not through a regex I wrote in the moment.
INSTRUMENT_LESSON_MY_OWN_GLOB_CHECKER.theBroaderPoint: This is the same failure this round keeps cataloguing, committed by me with a tool I built for the express purpose of not committing it. A cheap local reimplementation of a governed check is not the check — it is a second, unaudited instrument that happens to agree most of the time. The pre-write admission discipline is only worth having if it runs the REAL matcher.
INSTRUMENT_LESSON_MY_OWN_GLOB_CHECKER.whatItDidNotChange: My conclusion that the test paths were not MINE was correct under both matchers, so the disclosure itself stands. Only the attribution of who DOES own them was wrong.
